claims.statement: Complementary self-limiting vapor-surface reactions enable deposition of highly conformal coatings inside narrow holes.
Theoretical scaling laws predict the required exposure conditions based on the aspect ratio of the holes.
Diffusion of molecules down the hole limits the rate at which lower regions reach saturation compared to the flat surface.
Flux is reduced as precursor penetrates deeper along the coated length of the hole.
Film growth narrows the hole, increasing its aspect ratio during deposition.
Exposures exceeding 9000 Langmuir yielded 100% step coverage of HfO2 in agreement with model calculations.
Exposures below 9000 Langmuir failed to achieve 100% step coverage.
At large aspect ratios, the exposure required for conformality scales quadratically with aspect ratio.
Silicon-based microscopic lateral high-aspect-ratio test structures are introduced to analyze film conformality in ALD and CVD.
Microscopic LHAR test structures can analyze thin film conformality for ALD Al2O3 and TiO2 processes using various measurement methods.
Reactant decomposition and secondary side reactions decrease ALD film conformality in 3D structures.
Sub-micrometer channel heights ensure molecular flow regime inside microscopic LHAR structures under typical ALD pressures.
For Al2O3 ALD, penetration depth into the lateral channels increases as deposition temperature decreases.
For TiO2 ALD, the penetration depth non-monotonically first increases and then decreases with decreasing deposition temperature.
Waviness with a 10 µm period in the thickness profile is likely caused by the supporting oxide pillars.
Channel narrowing and closure near the entrance of the 200 nm gap restricted precursor penetration.
Visible/infrared transmission microscopy, reflectometry, and cross-sectional SEM give consistent qualitative penetration depth results.
Al2O3 films show flat saturation profiles terminating abruptly, whereas TiO2 films display continuous gradual thickness slopes.
Line scans of TiO2 film thickness show that the penetration depth in the lateral high-aspect-ratio structure increases with increasing channel gap size.
